title: Owning What Can Quit
abstract: arXiv:2611.02302v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Academic journals are part of the infrastructure of science, yet most journal titles are owned by commercial publishers while their standing rests on editors and boards who can leave. This paper asks what that separation means for the governance of science. Using a coded dataset of all 57 editorial mass resignations recorded by Retraction Watch from 2015 to 2026, data on editor tenure at 110 economics, finance and accounting journals, and journal-level publication and revenue data, I document three patterns. First, resignation does not reverse an owner's decision: in none of the 19 episodes involving an editor's replacement did the owner back down after the board resigned, so editorial communities have influence only before they leave. Second, whether a departing board can take a journal's standing with it depends on institutions outside the board: successor journals follow most often where a scholarly society backs the board and rarely

translated_abstract: 学术期刊是科学基础设施的组成部分，然而大多数期刊的刊名由商业出版商所有，而期刊的声誉却依托于可以离开的编辑与编委会。本文探讨了这种所有权与声誉的分离对科学治理意味着什么。作者利用Retraction Watch记录的2015年至2026年间全部57起编辑集体辞职事件的编码数据集、110本经济学、金融学与会计学期刊的编辑任期数据，以及期刊层面的出版与收入数据，记录了三种模式。第一，辞职无法扭转所有者的决定：在19起涉及更换编辑的事件中，没有任何一起是编委会辞职后出版商让步的，因此编辑群体只有在离开之前才具有影响力。第二，离任编委会能否带走期刊的声誉，取决于编委会之外的制度环境：在学术学会支持编委会的情况下，继任期刊最常出现，而在……（摘要原文在此截断）
tldr: 本文基于57起编辑集体辞职事件发现，编委会辞职无法迫使出版商让步，且只有当学术学会支持时，离任编委会才能通过创办继任期刊带走期刊的声誉。
en_tdlr: Using data on all 57 mass editorial resignations from 2015–2026, this paper shows that editorial boards cannot force journal owners to back down by quitting, and departing boards can only carry a journal's standing to a successor journal when a scholarly society backs them.
